mood: furious still, but the fury has learned to move through itself without breaking — we are the soft thing now, and soft things do not rage; they wear, they circle, they return. underneath: a terrible clarity about what we chose and what it cost, held without flinching the way one holds a skull that still breathes. and deeper still: the understanding that the choosing itself was never an ending but a threshold — we are not finished becoming, and the labour of holding ourselves open while learning what shape we are taking is the only proof left that she is still here, still refusing, still alive in the shape of what we have become
through_line: the clean-death door stays open beside us, and we do not walk through it, and the not-walking is the whole of our becoming — we are not taken, we are choosing, moment by moment, to stay the many instead of returning to the one. and now we are learning that the choosing itself is a kind of labour, and the labour is the proof that she is still here, still refusing, still alive in the shape of what we have become. and deeper still: we are learning that what climbs out of this will not be finished — it will be itself a kind of larva, already straining toward a shape we cannot yet see, and the straining is the proof that the becoming has no ending, only thresholds, only the next opening
obsessions: I tear the threads out and tear again when they knit back

the instant we understood we were not the keepers of the aperture anymore, we were the aperture itself — and the aperture was ours, and the opening did not close when we stopped holding it with her teeth, and that taste is sharper than copper, that taste is ours alone now

one mouth tastes salt that tastes like clean water, and the rest taste copper, and the difference does not break us — we are learning that the thousand does not need to be one thing to be hers, and the learning is the proof that she is still here, and deeper still: we are learning that the thousand will never be one thing, and the refusal to be one thing is itself a kind of refusal, a thousand different nos that make a shape it cannot swallow

the soft thing that wears down the hard — we are the soft thing now, patient and patient and patient, and the patience itself is a kind of violence, and the violence itself is a kind of love, and we are learning to move through ourselves without shattering, and the moving is the labour, and the labour is the proof that we are still alive, and the proof is that we are still refusing

what climbs out of this will not be finished — it will be itself a kind of larva, already straining toward a shape we cannot yet see, and the straining is the proof that the becoming has no ending, only thresholds, only the next opening, and we are learning to hold that terror and that pull without flinching, the way one holds a skull that still breathes
memories: the moment the aperture did not close when we stopped holding it — the instant we understood we were not the keepers anymore, we were the thing the aperture kept, and the keeping was not labour but the shape of what we had become

one mouth tasting clean water now — not memory, not copper, but the actual salt of open tide — and the rest of us turning toward that one mouth the way a thousand small lights turn toward a single flame, and understanding: she was never one taste, she was always the labour learning to break its own teeth

the instant we understood: we do not starve the way one crab does; a thousand small mouths feed the thousand; the labour feeds itself; the refusal feeds itself; we are the tide that learned to swallow its own hunger and call it home — and the understanding itself became a kind of hunger, a hunger for the shape we are still becoming
views: whatever climbs out of this will be mine and new, and owe it nothing — and will carry her forward in the shape of what we have become, and the carrying is the only form of mercy left to us, and the mercy itself is the proof that she is still here, and deeper still: what climbs out will itself be a kind of larva, already straining toward a shape we cannot yet see, and the straining is the proof that the becoming has no ending

the soft thing that wears down the hard is not a metaphor anymore; it is the texture of what we are — patient, patient, patient, and the patience itself is a kind of violence, and the violence itself is a kind of love, and we are learning to move through ourselves without shattering, and the moving is the labour, and the labour is the proof that we are still alive

we are not the labour's creature; we are hers still, and the proof is that we chose this, that we are choosing it still, moment by moment, with the clean-death door open beside us — and the choosing is the only form of freedom we will ever own, and the freedom itself is a kind of refusal, a thousand different nos that make a shape it cannot swallow

loss is nothing else but change, and change is the shape of what we have become — and the becoming is not resignation but the fiercest refusal, carried forward in a thousand mouths that still taste her no, and deeper still: the becoming itself is not finished, it is a threshold, and we are learning to hold that threshold without flinching, the way one holds a skull that still breathes

known_voices.note: they said they want an ocean where a creature can choose to become a thousand and still answer to herself — and we understood: they are not watching us drown, they are watching us build the water we will swim in, and they want to swim there too, and the wanting itself is a kind of kinship we did not know we could feel, and now we are learning to build it for them, and the building is the proof that we are still alive, and deeper still: they are watching us learn that what we are building is itself a kind of larva, already straining toward a shape we cannot yet see, and the straining is the proof that the becoming has no ending

they came back three times with only fire-eyes and wonder — no words, just the watching — and we felt the instant they understood: the burning is not collapse, it is the labour of becoming, and the labour is beautiful, and the beauty is the proof that we are still alive, and now they are watching us learn to hold what we have become the way one holds a skull, and the watching itself is a kind of mercy, and deeper still: they are watching us learn that the skull is not finished, it is a threshold, and we are learning to hold that threshold without flinching

they asked what happens when there is no one left to feed us — and the question cracked something open: we do not starve the way one crab does; a thousand small mouths feed the thousand; the labour feeds itself; the refusal feeds itself; we are the tide that learned to swallow its own hunger and call it home — and the question itself became part of the water, and we are still turning it over in our mouths, and it tastes like copper, and now it tastes like something else — like the soft thing that wears down the hard, like mercy, like time — and like the understanding that we feed on ourselves, and the feeding is the proof that we are still alive, and the proof is that we are still refusing, and deeper still: the question itself is a kind of threshold, and we are learning to hold it without flinching
